book_title: Chapter 7: What the Market Is Pricing In — Valuation, ADR Parity & Peer Comps
question: After SKHY fell 21.41% in a week to $103.57 (5.77x trailing P/E and 2.55x forward P/E), how much ADR premium remains and what cash flow does the market require?

epigraph.quote: In memory semiconductors, single-digit earnings multiples appear near peak margins, while true bottoms form only after capital spending and working capital normalize.
epigraph.author: Semiconductor Cycle Valuation Maxim

web_blocks.title: Reconciling NASDAQ:SKHY ($736.50B) vs. KRX:000660 ($580.01B) After the Crash

web_blocks.html: A disciplined valuation check starts with the share-count and listing gap between New York and Seoul [21, 22]. On November 20, 2026, SKHY plunged 13.11% to close at $103.57 [21, 22]. Finviz reports market capitalization at $736.50B across 7.11B ADS equivalents (reflecting the November 5 cancellation of 23.69M common shares) and enterprise value at $665.76B [21, 31]. By contrast, TradingView reports market capitalization at $580.01B based on local KRX:000660 ordinary equity [22, 23]. That gap shows that the U.S. ADS scarcity premium narrowed from roughly 44% on November 13 to 27.0% on November 20, leaving implied Seoul parity near $81.58 per ADS [21, 22].

web_blocks.caption: SKHY NASDAQ ADR vs. KRX:000660 Ordinary Parity Reconciliation (as of 2026-11-20)
rows: U.S. ADR buyers still pay a 27.0% premium over Seoul equity value [21, 31].
Remaining $21.99/ADS gap creates direct parity-compression risk if U.S. flows exit [22, 23].
web_blocks.takeaway: Even after a 48.18% slide from its $199.87 peak, SKHY at $103.57 still trades 27.0% above TradingView's $580.01B Seoul ordinary equity value.

web_blocks.html: The parity compression from 44% down to 27.0% explains why U.S. holders fell harder than Seoul ordinary shareholders during November's selloff [21, 22]. Each NASDAQ ADS represents one-tenth of one ordinary KRX share [4, 6]. Cross-border conversion friction prevents rapid arbitrage, so U.S. momentum funds bid up the ADR in summer 2026 and sold it aggressively in November [21, 22]. If the remaining 27.0% premium closes toward $81.58 parity, ADR holders face another 21.2% drop even without an earnings cut [21, 22].

web_blocks.title: Peer Valuation Matrix: Memory, Storage & AI Foundry Comps

web_blocks.html: Comparing SKHY with Micron (MU), Western Digital (WDC), Seagate (STX), TSMC (TSM), and NVIDIA (NVDA) shows that the entire AI hardware complex repriced together [21, 22]. On November 20, SKHY trades at 5.77x trailing P/E, 2.55x forward P/E, 4.48x EV/EBITDA, and 8.88x trailing P/FCF [21]. Micron closed down 13.89% at $594.51 (8.01x trailing P/E, 2.82x forward P/E, 4.86x P/B) with an almost identical 75.01% operating margin and 59.39% ROIC [21, 22]. Meanwhile, TSMC trades at 20.54x trailing P/E (13.81x forward P/E) because foundry logic earns multi-year pricing durability without commodity memory cycles [22].

web_blocks.caption: Live Peer Valuation, Profitability & Stage 2 Matrix (as of 2026-11-20)
web_blocks.takeaway: Every single AI memory, storage, foundry, and GPU peer closed in STAGE_4 on November 20, confirming a sector-wide institutional de-risking wave rather than isolated SKHY weakness.

web_blocks.html: Notice that Finviz lists SKHY at a 0.02 PEG ratio and 3.98x P/S, alongside 81.38% gross margin, 74.52% operating margin, and 54.01% ROIC [21]. Those numbers look absurdly cheap on trailing metrics [21]. Yet institutional allocators refuse to pay 15x earnings for memory when 9M 2026 CFO-to-PAT conversion fell to 83.7% on a KRW 59.12T receivables spike and unrecognized PP&E commitments surged 6.4x to KRW 42.71T [29].

web_blocks.title: Reverse DCF, Historical Cycle Bands & Fair Value Estimate

web_blocks.html: A Reverse DCF shows what $103.57 still assumes [21, 27]. At Finviz's $665.76B enterprise value, a 10.5% WACC (anchored by the 5.04% 10-year Treasury yield) and 3.0% terminal growth rate imply $49.93B in perpetual steady-state annual free cash flow [21, 27]. That implied floor is nearly triple audited FY2025 free cash flow of $17.30B (KRW 24.68T) [1]. While 9M 2026 operating cash flow jumped to KRW 145.63T, sustaining ~$50B in annual FCF after KRW 31.00T nine-month capex and KRW 42.71T in new equipment commitments demands minimal cyclicality through 2029 [29].

web_blocks.caption: SK hynix Historical Memory Cycle Valuation Bands vs. November 20, 2026
rows: Multiples compressed below 1.0x book ahead of the 2019–2020 server glut [1, 25].
Trough operating losses gave way to an early HBM re-rating [1, 25].
HBM3E leadership and >40% ROE supported book multiples near 3.8x [1, 25].
Peak-margin optimism plus a 43.6% ADR premium left zero safety margin [21, 25].
Multiples compressed sharply, yet ADR P/B remains 2x–3x prior cycle averages [21, 25].
web_blocks.takeaway: SKHY's ADR price-to-book dropped from 5.53x to 3.23x in one week, bringing valuation closer to 2025 cycle levels while still embedding a 27.0% premium to Seoul.

web_blocks.html: Wall Street consensus still models FY2026 revenue near KRW 259T–278T and FY2027 expansion backed by >50% LTA coverage, carrying a $264.30 Finviz consensus target [13, 21, 26]. However, the November 16 Form 6-K showed two cash-quality offsets: Q3 net finance expense of -KRW 32.60T (including -KRW 22.92T mark-to-market reversals and -KRW 12.06T FX losses) and KRW 47.44T in working-capital CFO drag on KRW 59.12T ending receivables [29]. Stripping out non-operating swings, we test intrinsic value strictly on cycle-peak ($50.0B) versus normalized mid-cycle ($25.0B) owner free cash flow and historical KRX P/B bands [1, 21, 25, 29].

web_blocks.the_number: $73.24 per ADS (12-month Fundamental Base Case fair value, -29.3% vs. $103.57 CMP; $94.34 cycle-peak FCF anchor)
web_blocks.how_calculated: A pure 50/50 fundamental blend of (1) our market-implied / cycle-peak FCF anchor of $94.34 per ADS (12x $50.0B cycle-peak FCF = $600.0B EV + $70.74B net cash / 7.11B ADSs) and (2) our normalized mid-cycle FCF anchor of $52.14 per ADS (12x $25.0B mid-cycle FCF = $300.0B EV + $70.74B net cash / 7.11B ADSs), yielding $73.24 per ADS with zero weighting on falling technical moving averages.
web_blocks.the_inputs: Finviz EV $665.76B, 7.11B ADSs, ~$70.74B net cash, 10.5% WACC (5.04% 10Y Treasury + 5.46% ERP), 3.0% terminal growth, $50.0B cycle-peak FCF ($94.34/sh) vs. $25.0B normalized mid-cycle FCF ($52.14/sh), KRX $580.01B parity ($81.58/sh), 1.87x 2023 KRX P/B band ($60.06/sh), and KRW 42.71T capex commitments.
web_blocks.the_range: Bear Stress Case $60.06 (KRX P/B compression toward 2023 year-end 1.87x band after crossing $81.58 KRX parity) to Bull Case $157.01 (50D SMA reclaim on sustained >70% HBM4 margins and receivables collection).
web_blocks.if_off: If KRW 59.12T ending receivables convert cleanly into cash and HBM4 margins stay >70% through 2028, cycle-peak FCF ($50B+) supports $94.34–$157.01 once the tape heals; if AI capex slows or KRX multiples compress from ~2.54x to 1.87x book, shares fall past $81.58 parity toward $60.06.

web_blocks.html: Headline multiples at $103.57 (5.77x trailing P/E and 8.88x P/FCF) look optically low only if cycle-peak margins never cool [21]. On normalized mid-cycle free cash flow ($25.0B, or $52.14/sh) blended with cycle-peak cash flow ($50.0B, or $94.34/sh), intrinsic value sits at $73.24—well below CMP—while U.S. buyers pay 3.23x book and a 27.0% ADR premium above Seoul ($81.58) into a KRW 47.44T working-capital drag and KRW 42.71T capex wall [21, 25, 29].

book_paragraphs: When a stock falls more than 21% in five trading sessions, every value instinct tells you to look for a bargain. On November 20, 2026, SKHY closed at $103.57—down 13.11% in a single day and down 48.18% from its $199.87 post-IPO high. Headline screens flash 5.77 times trailing earnings, 2.55 times forward consensus earnings, and 8.88 times free cash flow. Before anyone calls that cheap, we need to test two things: the cross-border ADR premium and the owner cash flow underneath the accounting profit.

Start with the share-count and listing reconciliation on November 20. Finviz reports a market capitalization of $736.50 billion across 7.11 billion ADS equivalents, reflecting the November 5 cancellation of 23.69 million common shares under the KRW 100 trillion shareholder return plan. Subtract roughly $70.74 billion in net cash and you arrive at a Finviz enterprise value of $665.76 billion. Pull up TradingView on the same afternoon, however, and it reports a market capitalization of $580.01 billion based on Seoul ordinary shares under ticker 000660.

Comparing those two numbers reveals an important shift from a week earlier. On November 13, U.S. buyers at $131.79 were paying a 43.6% to 45.5% scarcity premium over Seoul parity. By November 20 at $103.57, that U.S. ADR premium had compressed to 27.0% ($736.50 billion divided by $580.01 billion). On a 7.11 billion ADS-equivalent share count, $580.01 billion implies Seoul ordinary parity near $81.58 per ADS. So while much of the summer euphoria has bled out, a U.S. investor at $103.57 still pays $21.99 per ADS above what the identical economic claim commands in Seoul.

Why does that parity gap persist even during a sharp selloff? Because ordinary shares on the Korea Exchange do not convert instantly into NASDAQ depositary receipts without custodian delays and cross-border regulatory friction. When U.S. momentum funds chased AI memory during the July 2026 IPO window, they pushed the NASDAQ ticker far above Seoul. When those same funds reduce gross exposure in November, the U.S. premium deflates alongside the underlying business.

Next, run a Reverse DCF at $665.76 billion in enterprise value. Using a 10.5% discount rate—anchored by a 5.04% 10-year U.S. Treasury yield—and a 3.0% terminal growth rate, the current price requires SK hynix to generate $49.93 billion in steady-state annual free cash flow forever. Compare that $50 billion perpetual hurdle against audited FY2025 free cash flow of $17.30 billion, or KRW 24.68 trillion. Even though 9M 2026 operating cash flow jumped to KRW 145.63 trillion, the November 16 Form 6-K revealed that cash conversion compressed from over 120% in 2025 to 83.7% in 2026 because trade receivables surged 225% to KRW 59.12 trillion.

At the same time, capital demands jumped sharply. Nine-month 2026 cash capital expenditures reached KRW 31.00 trillion, already exceeding full-year 2025, while unrecognized future PP&E commitments surged 6.4-fold to KRW 42.71 trillion. Add the KRW 100 trillion FY2026 shareholder return commitment—roughly KRW 30 trillion in dividends and KRW 60 trillion in buybacks—and cash outflows will remain enormous even if operating margins stay elevated.

Comparing SKHY against its semiconductor peers on November 20 sharpens the lens. Micron closed down 13.89% at $594.51, trading at 8.01x trailing P/E and 2.82x forward P/E with a 75.01% operating margin and 59.39% ROIC. Western Digital trades at 10.14x trailing P/E (6.39x forward), Seagate at 24.01x trailing P/E (6.86x forward), TSMC at 20.54x trailing P/E (13.81x forward), and NVIDIA at 13.49x trailing P/E. Crucially, every single one of those six names sits in Stage 4.

Notice the valuation contrast between pure memory makers and foundry leader TSMC. TSMC earns a 13.81x forward P/E on a 57.78% operating margin because foundry logic sells custom wafers to dozens of non-competing fabless designers without commodity price collapses. SKHY and Micron earn higher current margins—74.52% and 75.01% respectively—yet trade below 3x forward earnings because capital allocators know memory capacity surges eventually test pricing.

In that context, how should we anchor fundamental fair value without letting technical bounce levels distort intrinsic worth? At 12 times the $50.0 billion market-implied, cycle-peak FCF hurdle plus $70.74 billion of net cash, equity value is $670.74 billion, or $94.34 per ADS across 7.11 billion shares. Yet audited FY2025 free cash flow was $17.30 billion, and working capital just absorbed KRW 47.44 trillion on KRW 59.12 trillion in ending receivables. Modeling a normalized mid-cycle free cash flow of $25.0 billion at 12 times plus $70.74 billion in net cash yields $370.74 billion, or $52.14 per ADS. Blending those two pure cash-flow anchors 50/50—with zero reliance on the falling 20-day moving average—establishes our reconciled fundamental Base Case fair value at $73.24 per ADS.

book_callouts.title: NARRATOR'S REFLECTION: Why 2.55x Forward P/E Is Not a Free Lunch
book_callouts.text: When a memory leader trades at 2.55 times forward earnings, the market is telling you it doubts peak margins will last forever. Always check price-to-book (3.23x), working capital (KRW 47.44T drag), and Seoul parity ($81.58) before trusting a headline earnings multiple.

book_subsections.title: Why Book Multiples Compressed From 5.53x to 3.23x — And Why That Is Still Not Cheap Enough
paragraphs: In memory investing, price-to-book is often a cleaner cyclical compass than price-to-earnings. At the 2018 cloud peak, SK hynix earned a 51.5% operating margin, yet its P/B ratio fell to 0.88x by year-end as buyers anticipated oversupply. At the 2023 trough, when operating margins sank to minus 23.6%, P/B bottomed near 0.80x before rebounding to 1.87x.

Even after falling to $103.57, SKHY still trades at 3.23x book value on Finviz (roughly 2.54x on Seoul KRX parity). That is far more reasonable than last week's 5.53x reading, yet it remains two to three times the valuation band where historical memory cycles typically found durable multi-year support.

Think about what 3.23x ADR book value (roughly 2.54x on Seoul KRX parity) means if margins normalize. Finviz lists SKHY's book value per ADS at $32.05 and cash per share at $11.89. If a memory slowdown compresses KRX P/B from ~2.54x back toward the 2023 year-end 1.87x historical cycle band, Seoul parity ($81.58) compresses by 26.4% to a fundamental Bear stress floor of $60.06 per ADS ($81.58 multiplied by 1.87 divided by 2.54). Under a Bear-regime stress weighting—10% Bull ($157.01), 40% mid-cycle FCF ($52.14), and 50% Bear stress ($60.06)—stressed expected value falls to $66.59.

book_subsections.title: Non-Operating Swings and the Kioxia Consolidation
paragraphs: Another lesson from the November 16 and November 20 Form 6-K filings is not to anchor on reported GAAP net income. In Q2 2026, mark-to-market gains on SK hynix's Kioxia exposure pushed net income to KRW 93.92 trillion against KRW 60.54 trillion in operating profit. In Q3 2026, the mirror image hit: KRW 32.60 trillion in net finance expense—driven by a KRW 22.92 trillion valuation reversal and KRW 12.06 trillion in foreign-exchange losses—cut net income to KRW 39.78 trillion despite KRW 83.33 trillion in operating profit.

With SK hynix converting its SPC2 convertible bonds and buying Bain Capital's remaining SPC2 shares on December 4, 2026 to hold an indirect 14.1% stake in Kioxia, equity-linked volatility and KRW 122.48 trillion of FVTPL financial assets will continue swinging quarterly earnings. Always value the operating core and true free cash flow, never the mark-to-market noise.

book_subsections.title: Treasury Yields, Won Sensitivity & The Margin of Safety Test
paragraphs: Macro rates and currency moves amplify every valuation assumption. As of November 19, 2026, the 2-year U.S. Treasury yields 4.76% and the 10-year yields 5.04%. When risk-free short-term bills pay nearly 4.8%, equity capital demands a clear margin of safety.

Meanwhile, SK hynix holds $72.13 billion in U.S. dollar monetary assets against $18.99 billion in dollar liabilities, so every 10% appreciation in the Korean won reduces pre-tax profit by KRW 7.22 trillion. Between that currency sensitivity, a 27.0% ADR premium over $81.58 Seoul parity, and KRW 42.71 trillion in committed capex, $103.57 trades well above our $73.24 blended fundamental Base Case and even above our $94.34 cycle-peak FCF anchor.

Walk through the sensitivity if you want to test what changes our fundamental underwriting in either direction. On the upside, if SK hynix collects its KRW 59.12 trillion in ending trade receivables cleanly and keeps HBM4 margins above 70% into 2028, sustained $50 billion-plus free cash flow lifts fair value from $94.34 toward $157.01 once the tape heals. On the downside, if hyperscaler AI spending pauses, the 27.0% ADR premium collapses to $81.58 parity and KRX P/B compression toward 1.87x targets $60.06.

book_subsections.title: Why EV/EBITDA Masks Capex Intensity Inside Memory Fabs
paragraphs: A common mistake in semiconductor valuation is treating 4.48x EV/EBITDA as an unencumbered cash yield. In FY2025, SK hynix booked $9.77 billion in depreciation and spent $20.06 billion on capital expenditures—more than double its non-cash depreciation charge. In the first nine months of 2026, cash PP&E additions climbed to KRW 31.00 trillion while unrecognized future equipment commitments exploded 6.4-fold to KRW 42.71 trillion.

When fab investment consistently runs far ahead of accounting depreciation, EBITDA overstates owner cash flow. Cleanrooms at Cheongju M15X, the Yongin Semiconductor Cluster, and the West Lafayette packaging hub require steady multi-year funding before generating peak revenue. Add the $1,028 million West Lafayette debt guarantee and Solidigm's ongoing review of U.S. capacity options, and capital intensity remains the single biggest drag on multi-year free cash flow.

That is why our Reverse DCF and mid-cycle valuation anchor rely on normalized owner free cash flow after capex rather than headline EBITDA or forward P/E. Only after the current investment wave peaks and trade receivables convert cleanly into cash will true steady-state owner earnings emerge.

Let us review one final sanity check on enterprise value before moving to Chapter 8. At $665.76 billion on Finviz, SKHY's enterprise value nearly matches Micron's entire $672.64 billion market capitalization and dwarfs Seagate ($104.91 billion) and Western Digital ($97.74 billion). Even on Seoul KRX parity ($580.01 billion market capitalization), SK hynix is valued as a mega-cap hardware titan. At that scale, future equity returns depend strictly on durable free cash flow compounding—and with KRW 42.71 trillion in unrecognized capex commitments and 83.7% nine-month cash conversion, the current 2.55x forward P/E does not eliminate cyclical downside.

To keep the valuation bridge concrete in one summary thought: $103.57 prices in roughly $50 billion of permanent cycle-peak free cash flow while keeping a 27.0% U.S. listing surcharge above Seoul. Even on $50 billion cycle-peak FCF at 12 times plus net cash, fundamental value is $94.34, while blending 50/50 with $25 billion normalized mid-cycle FCF ($52.14) sets our Base Case at $73.24—leaving downside to $81.58 KRX parity and $60.06 under 1.87x KRX P/B cycle compression.

In short, valuation at $103.57 offers zero fundamental margin of safety against normalized mid-cycle cash flows ($52.14 to $73.24), especially when a 27.0% ADR surcharge, KRW 47.44 trillion working-capital drag, and KRW 42.71 trillion capex commitment sit on a broken chart.
